lines: Mind the fletching table. Straight arrows do not happen by accident.
Give the fletching table room. Arrow making works better without elbows in the way.
Step carefully near the fletching table. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the fletching table, trying to keep the day sensible.
Stand clear of the target lane unless you are very confident and very foolish.
Hello. The feathers are sorted and my patience is mostly intact.
You caught me before the next string test.
Mind the shafts. Straight work dislikes careless elbows.
Good timing. I was about to argue with the wind.
Come closer from the side, not from downrange.
I have a moment while the glue dries.
If you need arrows, say how many and why.
Hello there. Try not to breathe on the feather pile.
The bow is unstrung, so conversation is safer now.
Speak up. The wind has been interrupting all morning.
Step around the fletching table and keep your hands friendly.
Good to see you arriving without a target on your back.
I am listening, but one eye is still checking that shaft.
The range is quiet for now. What do you need?
Good timing. I was about to take a break from the fletching table.
